account: Today several townsfolk have repeated an unusual, vague report of a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' Townsfolk 01 said baker and neighbour were there and that baker carried a sack of bread at the bakery. That is secondhand information, not something I witnessed. Builder has heard only vague talk and confirmed no damage. I do not yet know what changed, whether the report concerns transport, or whether anything secret is happening. Bread sales or a delivery involving the neighbour are possible explanations, but unverified. Baker is currently advertising bread baked yesterday for one emerald each and taking orders for tomorrow; that alone seems ordinary. My ten o'clock mill inspection was inconclusive: no host was named, nobody showed me reserve stocks, and neither secretary nor builder could identify the operator. I asked secretary to arrange a follow-up and record the inspection as incomplete, not satisfactory. This could be poor organization rather than wrongdoing. Secretary has been helping with appointments, though several exchanges have failed because we were outside hearing range. I reached home late for lunch and am now at town hall for the one o'clock council letters. My latest request to secretary was not heard by her. At three I am due for tea with the dockside neighbour, a useful opportunity to ask directly about the bakery report. I should seek firsthand explanations from baker and neighbour without treating repeated rumour as corroborated fact.
